Definition: an extremity; adverbially (with prepositional prefix) after
BiblicalUsage: God tells Noah the end of all flesh is come, and Amos hears that the end is come upon Israel. The Preacher says there is no end of all the people, and Daniel is told to go his way till the end, for he shall rest and stand in his lot at the end of the days. The word is the extremity — the far edge of things, where God draws the line.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe every end in Scripture belongs to God, and the end he sets is not a wall but a door. I hold that Daniel was told to rest and stand in his lot at the end of the days, and that promise is for all who wait.
